title: As a founder, I get a real street address (not a PO Box) that works for LLC registration, bank KYC, and vendor forms
As a founder, I can complete USPS Form 1583 with guided help — pre-filled forms, online notarization, and clear ID requirements — instead of deciphering the CMRA process alone
As a founder, I can get documentation that banks and payment processors accept as proof of business address, with the provider stating where the address works and where it doesn't
As a founder, I can choose the address's state and city to match my entity strategy — Delaware, Wyoming, my home state — from clearly listed locations
As an operator, my mail is opened and scanned to searchable PDFs with a stated turnaround — same or next business day — not just an envelope photo
As an operator, scans are OCR'd and my mail archive is searchable by sender, content, and date
As an operator, I control what happens to the physical mail — documented storage windows, on-request shredding with confirmation, and per-item disposal choices
As an operator, I can forward mail with rules or one click — saved recipients, carrier choice, and cost shown before I confirm — rather than emailing support
As a digital nomad, the address accepts packages from all major carriers and can consolidate or hold them for pickup or forwarding
As a founder, checks that arrive in the mail get deposited to my bank account by the provider — endorsed, deposited, and reconciled without the paper touching my hands
As a founder, check deposit terms are published — supported banks, per-deposit fees, turnaround time, and what happens to the physical check afterward
As a founder, I can get registered agent service tied to the same account — service-of-process handling bundled with or added to my mailbox plan
As a founder, I can pair the address with entity services — LLC formation, lease-grade addresses for foreign qualification, or residency-grade addresses — from the same provider
As an operator, government and legal mail — IRS, state filings, service of process — is flagged or prioritized so a compliance deadline never sits unread in the pile
As a developer, I can list mail items and download scans through a documented public API — my systems ingest postal mail like any other data source
As a developer, I get webhooks (or at least Zapier triggers) when new mail arrives or a scan completes, so downstream automation starts without polling
As an operator, I can export my scans and mail history in bulk — PDFs and metadata leave the platform when I do
As a founder, plan pricing is public and complete — monthly price, scan allowances, and the per-item fees for extra scans, forwarding, storage, and check deposit
As a digital nomad, I can pick from a broad network of locations — multiple states and countries — and see each location's capabilities before signing up
As an operator, the provider documents how mail is physically secured and digitally protected — facility controls, staff screening, encryption of scans
As an operator, I can reach a human about a specific piece of mail — real support channels with stated response expectations, because a lost check isn't a chatbot problem
